title: Lambda for slope and y-intercept
description:
Write a lambda function which can solve a slope or y-intercept of linear functions.

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as `slope_and_intercept(x1, y1, x2, y2)`, using lambda functions internally to compute the slope `m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1)` and the y-intercept `b = y1 - m * x1` of the line through the two points `(x1, y1)` and `(x2, y2)`, returning the tuple `(m, b)`.
hints: The slope of a line through two points is `(y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1)`.
Once you have the slope `m`, the y-intercept is `y1 - m * x1`.
Define each formula as a `lambda` (e.g. `lambda x1, y1, x2, y2: (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1)`) and call them to build the returned tuple `(m, b)`.
expected_behavior: Returns a tuple (slope, y_intercept) for the line passing through the two given points, computed using lambda functions.

hidden_tests.label: simple positive slope through the y-axis

explanation: One lambda computes the slope from the rise-over-run formula `(y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1)`, and a second lambda plugs that slope into `y1 - m * x1` to get the y-intercept. Both lambdas are called immediately and their results returned together as a tuple.
